question.worked_solution:
We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(1.12<Z<2.02).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14254773/assets/d6fdd07c42136419e9e76466840386710f685cec82f7de1f6081c540bbe07a6c.png)

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$ 

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

So, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1.12<Z<2.02) & =P(Z<2.02)-P(Z\le 1.12) \\  & =P(Z\le 2.02)-P(Z\le 1.12) \\  & =Φ(2.02)-Φ(1.12).\end{aligned}
$$

From the tables, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(1.12) & =0.8686 \\ Φ(2.02) & =0.9783\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1.12<Z<2.02) & =Φ(2.02)-Φ(1.12) \\  & =0.9783-0.8686 \\  & =0.1097.\end{aligned}
$$
